FINAL READ-ONLY REVIEW — PR #665, exact head b205724dd39f922bd70a060de3489c98f765b484 (commits 9c0ed7b6 and b205724d), scratch branch eshyra-olc5.12.5. Profile: rules-clause-complete / semantic-system. Reviewed the full origin/main...HEAD change, both commits, live PR, owning capability/contract, both dispatch reports, c58j/.12.3/.12.4, faithful-or-absent decision, repository review/importer policy and ADRs 0017/0020. The refs/beads/state projection is stale (2026-09-09 and lacks .12); current live bd records governed this review. Source checks used the vendored SRD PDF and generated records, including Conjure Elemental (p.128), Efreeti Bottle (p.220/table continuation), Figurines (pp.221–223), and Ring of Djinni Summoning (p.235).

S1 — P1 blocking — Grant identity is not grounded to the exact source instance.
Location: packages/core/src/state/activeEffects.ts:3804 (also :4025, :4074); packages/core/src/orchestrator/toolStartEffect.ts:351.
Invariant/authority: the selected capability binds a printed grant to its actual inventory instance; ADR 0020 requires real identity bindings and fail-closed unrecognized inputs; faithful-or-absent forbids a source-backed claim for a different item.
Concrete failures, independently probed through the actual start_effect tool with the bundled pack: (a) install variantId onyx-dog, then bind grantRef bronze-griffon to a griffon; accepted, itemDurationBinding.status bound, six-hour typed timer. effectiveMagicItemMechanics does not filter the parent entityGrant list: all figurine grants are parent-scoped and the variants have no mechanics. Reading variant_id therefore supplies no actual grant-to-variant check. This is a creature-identity error, not the excluded exclusivity/control policy. (b) source {kind:magic-item, grantRef:nonexistent}, with no ref or itemInstanceId and an until-removed duration, is accepted; item_grant_json is NULL. The presence-only grantRef gate is bypassed because both binding validators skip sources without ref.
Required closure: every declared item-grant binding must resolve the printed grant on the actual instance/selected source variant; a dangling declaration must refuse, or use the explicit ruling path, rather than silently become an unbound magic-item summon. Permanent evidence: generalized source/instance/variant admission invariant, with source-backed figurine memberships and negative missing-ref/unknown-grant cases. This preserves the printed identity claim more effectively than another wrong-creature example. Material repair; owner .12; repair before approval.

S2 — P1 blocking — Item concentration ignores the retained Conjure Elemental pointer and accepts unprinted concentration endings.
Location: packages/core/src/state/activeEffects.ts:3907 and :4514; createUncontrolledSuccessor at :3090 only admits spell sources.
Invariant/authority: .12 explicitly includes elemental vessels with the conjure-elemental concentration exception; magicItemTriage.ts:35 deliberately retains as spell:conjure-elemental to carry that exception. The SRD spell says concentration is required, its break leaves the elemental present, and an uncontrolled elemental disappears one hour after summoning. Those are deterministic lifetime semantics; excluded obedience/hostility interpretation does not authorize deleting the creature.
Probe: bind the real Bowl water-elemental grant without concentrationOwner: accepted. Bind it with a character concentrationOwner and end_effect concentration-broken/voluntary: accepted, cleanupOnBreak defaults remove, elemental status becomes absent, and no uncontrolled successor exists. Same mechanism affects all four vessels and Elemental Gem. The converse also fails: an Onyx Dog grant accepts a concentrationOwner and disappears when that concentration is voluntarily broken, although the printed figurine has no concentration requirement.
Required closure: derive required/forbidden concentration and exceptional break/continuing-deadline behavior from the retained source contract; do not turn the exceptional survival rule into ordinary removal or leave an unowned permanent elemental. Permanent evidence: generalized ordinary-versus-exceptional concentration lifecycle invariant over real pack carriers, including refusal of unprinted concentration on a figurine. Material repair; owner .12; repair before approval.

S3 — P1 blocking — A bound grant can end while its creature remains in play.
Location: packages/core/src/state/activeEffects.ts:3914, :4514 and :4653–4678.
Invariant/authority: typed reversion/existence endings in .12 must remove the granted creature through the existing lifecycle. A grant-ended anchor is justified by the actual departure/return, not merely by ending a bookkeeping row.
Probe with no readiness waiver: bind Onyx Dog with actors[].cleanupOnEnd release; advanceWorldTime 360 minutes. The effect ends expired but campaign_actor dog stays alive, rather than reverting at its printed six-hour limit. Anchored sibling: a paid Ring summon accepts cleanupOnEnd release and cleanupOnBreak release; end_effect leaves djinni alive while scheduling the ring cooldown at 1440. Grant admission checks atZeroHitPoints but does not constrain these policies; spell-only cleanup derivation never supplies a grant policy.
Required closure: a bound existence-ending grant must enforce its printed removal policy (and its applicable exceptional break policy); a contradictory house-rule/ruling must not retain an ordinary source binding and falsely emit departure. Permanent evidence: generalized actor-presence/terminal-event invariant covering timer, concentration and explicit end, with release-policy refusals where removal is printed. Material repair; owner .12; repair before approval.

S4 — P2 should-fix — Grant cooldowns start at the clock-sweep endpoint instead of the actual expiry deadline.
Location: packages/core/src/state/activeEffects.ts:3018–3028 (caller :7091); packages/core/src/state/itemState.ts:2028.
Invariant/authority: .12/.8 require 24 hours from grant end; SRD Ring cooldown starts after the djinni departs, and the Efreeti stopper wait starts after service returns it to the bottle. Clock advancement must settle due events within its elapsed interval.
Probe using the documented readiness waiver only for the gated spend: summon the Ring djinni at elapsed 0 (deadline 60), then advanceWorldTime by 2880 minutes. The effect expires but the economy is {remaining:0, availableAt:4320}; it should have become available at 1500 and already reset by 2880. finalizeEnd passes neither the actual expiry minute nor an equivalent event time, so applyItemCooldownAnchorEvent reads the advanced clock. Efreeti serving expiry has the identical defect. Exact-boundary tests at 60 minutes do not distinguish it.
Required closure: carry the effective termination time through expiry and cascaded endings and settle newly due resets correctly in the same interval. Permanent evidence: generalized partition-invariance check (one large advance versus advances split at the source deadline and cooldown deadline) for both anchored carriers. Proportionate because this is the newly landed F5 resource-accounting claim. Material repair; owner .12; repair before approval.

S5 — P2 should-fix — refresh_effect bypasses the newly bound grant duration and retains false typed provenance.
Location: packages/core/src/state/activeEffects.ts:4145 (new binding) and :6821–6858 (refresh consumer).
Invariant/authority: .12 requires the effect duration to equal the typed grant duration unless an explicit override is recorded. A durable source binding and provenance cannot silently become false through another public mutation.
Probe through production tools with the unmodified pack: bind Onyx Dog (six hours); refresh_effect with timed 24 hours/effect-created succeeds. The stored/view duration becomes 24 hours while durationProvenance remains {kind:typed-fixed, amount:6, unit:hour}. Ring similarly changes from one to 24 hours; until-removed can remove the timer entirely. Refresh currently revalidates spell durations only.
Required closure: make refresh preserve a grant's source duration/renewal constraints or explicitly record an authorized unbound override; do not retain stale typed-fixed evidence. Permanent evidence: generalized bound-duration/provenance consistency across creation and refresh, including duration-kind changes and the existing explicit-override path. This tests the actual mutation boundary, not just constructor rejection. Material repair; owner .12; repair before approval.

S6 — P2 should-fix — The known Goat of Traveling grant cannot bind at all.
Location: packages/core/src/state/activeEffects.ts:3892–3896.
Invariant/authority: the binding design permits untyped/null durations to be DM-adjudicated; the kept grant category includes this printed creature. SRD pp.222–223 gives hour-or-portion charge consumption rather than a fixed existence duration. The current pack consequently has duration absent and revertOn duration-ended.
Probe: install ivory-goats; link a real riding-horse combatant with campaignActorId; provide a DM-selected one-hour timer. start_effect refuses with "ends on duration-ended but has no typed duration to end on". An until-removed declaration also cannot satisfy this branch. The census test merely checks that duration-ended is a key in the map; it does not show this carrier can use that disposition.
Required closure: reconcile the known printed charge-driven lifetime with the promised adjudicated-duration binding, without inventing a fixed cap. The exclusion in .12.3 concerns spend coupling, not total refusal of this grant. Permanent evidence: source-backed regression for this irregular no-fixed-duration grant, within a broader admissibility check for kept timer dispositions. Material repair/design reconciliation; owner .12; repair before approval.

S7 — P1 blocking — Expiring a grant can freeze an otherwise valid add-on campaign's world clock.
Location: packages/core/src/state/activeEffects.ts:3016 / :2868; packages/core/src/state/rest.ts:216–222.
Invariant/authority: ADR 0020 preserves state-integrity guarantees and real campaign rules bindings; existing campaignRecordLookup resolves the whole exact stack through the supplied CampaignRulesPackResolver. Adding a grant-ended integration must preserve that context on every terminal path.
Probe without any readiness waiver: install an Onyx Dog, bind a valid empty compatible add-on in campaign_rules_binding, supply a resolver for base plus add-on, and bind its six-hour grant successfully. advanceWorldTime(60) succeeds. advanceWorldTime(300), reaching expiry, throws "campaign rules pack 'dnd5e-srd' / 'review-addon' @ '1.0.0' is unavailable"; the transaction rolls back, clock remains 60 and effect active. rest.ts drops resolveRulesPack when calling expireElapsedWorldEffects. The new finalizeEnd lookup now resolves the whole stack even for this unanchored grant, so a previously valid expiry acquires an unavailable-source failure. An anchored Ring probe fails the same way.
Required closure: propagate the exact campaign resolver through terminal/cascade callers that now consult item mechanics (including world time and life-event callers), preserving atomic rollback for real refusals without refusing a valid available stack. Permanent evidence: generalized rules-stack parity across explicit end, expiry and life-event endings with an available add-on. This is proportionate to a failure that can block clock/rest/HP progression. Material repair; owner .12; repair before approval.

Coverage and dispositions: reviewed all current revertOn values and the actual end paths (world/round expiry, 0 HP, concentration, end_effect, encounter closure and suppression). The terminal status claim is idempotent in the exercised cases: suppression schedules nothing; subsequent concentration end schedules once; repeating that end returns changed:false and leaves one ended ledger event. Persistent campaign-actor rebinding survives closure in the ordinary tested case; it does not cure S2/S3/S7. Count/creature/duration refusals, spent/unscheduled coupling and duplicate-live-binding checks are otherwise present. Deliberate non-anchored economy coupling, control/obedience/hostility, capture/crafting, illusion/object behavior and Efreeti outcome/counter work remain the declared exclusions; they are not findings here. No requirement: deterministic item death-consequence modeling beyond the deliberately adjudicated death-consequence clauses. No requirement: the advisory Efreeti hint itself resolving the excluded random outcome.

Migration 0047/snapshot and migration-adoption evidence agree. The Efreeti operation's printed action sentence is source-backed; generated changes are confined to Efreeti Bottle and Ring. Census/readiness movements correspond to that operation and hook. Independent deriveItemOperationReadinessInput + assertMagicItemOperationReady enumeration found 13 ready operation/variant identities before and after, newly ready [] and no-longer-ready []; the stated zero delta is accurate. Readiness-gated spends were waived only in staged anchored-lifecycle probes, as explicitly noted above; S1/S2/S3/S5/S6/S7 also exercise the live start_effect surface without such a waiver. The landed F5 claim is not yet established for both carriers because of S3/S4/S7; absence of newly ready use_item operations lowers exposure for the staged spend cases but does not waive the accepted responsibility.

Verification: direct Vitest run of itemGrantSummons, migrationLegacyAdoption, persistence: 41/41 passed. Compiler, triage, owner-tag conservation, legacy backlog, generated-pack suites: 354/354 passed. Total 395 focused tests passed. npm run verify:dnd5e-srd-pack exited 0: zero manifest/record drift and exact source inventory/coverage/region/provenance/relationship matches. Existing tests do not distinguish the bad states above. All probes ran from stdin against in-memory SQLite; no probe files were created. Tree remains clean. PR remains open at the exact requested head; all reported GitHub checks are successful. No source edits, commits, push, PR comments/review/merge, parent-bead changes or beads sync were performed.

STOP CONDITION: these concrete identity and lifetime/concentration failures concern the KEPT grant category after two implementation attempts. Surface this evidence to the user under the owning bead's STOP CONDITION before authorizing further repair work; do not silently demote the category or start another narrow repair based only on the existing example tests. Required next state is repair/design reconciliation and fresh review of the material changes, not approval of this head.

VERDICT: BLOCKING
